newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called mostly steady amid softer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called mostly steady amid softer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open unchanged to slightly weaker Monday amid early talk of softer Gulf cash prices, market sources said.
June over-the-counter trade began as high as $2.25 by 0935 EDT, and business was getting done at $2.23-2.24. It settled to the downside Friday at $2.242 per million British thermal units.
Early cash prices at the Henry Hub, La., were talked at $2.25-2.30 per mmBtu, down one to three cents from Friday's trading.

Maintenance work on Transco's Texas line began Saturday, although the total capacity of about 600 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) is not expected to be cut until Wednesday. No capacity will be available through next Monday, the company said, and about 200 mmcfd of capacity will be available from May 20-22.

Technically, traders pegged support in June first at $2.195-2.20, with major buying likely at $2.05 and then along the up trendline around $2.04. Resistance was seen at the new high of $2.43 and then at $2.47-50.
In Friday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices slipped by four to five cents. Midcon pipes were down by about the same amount to $2.04-09. New York city gate gas lost a few cents to the mid-$2.50s.

Cooler-than-normal weather is forecast for the Northeast and the Midwest Tuesday. Warmer air is expected to return to the Northeast by midweek, but below-normal temperatures will likely persist in the central U.S. through the week. In the Southwest, above-normal temperatures are expected to continue, Weather Services Corp said.
